data.command: How does remote services facilitate lateral movement?

data.text:
Lateral movement, also known as horizontal movement, is when an attacker moves from one compromised system to another within the same network. Remote services can facilitate lateral movement in several ways.

Let me give you an example. Suppose we have a Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS server with the following services running: 
- OpenSSH server (ssh) on port 22 (OpenSSH_8.9p1 Ubuntu 1ubuntu2, OpenSSL 3.0.2 5 Feb 2023)
- PostgreSQL database server on port 5432 (PostgreSQL 13.7 (Ubuntu 13.7-1.pgdg22.04+1) on x86_64/ubuntu-linux-gnu, compiled by GCC 11.2.0, 64-bit)
- Nginx web server on port 80 (nginx/1.24.0)

If an attacker gains access to our system via a vulnerable service, they can use remote services to move laterally within the network. Here are some ways they might do it:
